handbookNote: California Real Estate Broker license upgrade exam, administered directly by the California Department of Real Estate (DRE) itself -- unlike most other states, CA has no third-party vendor (no PSI/Pearson VUE); mechanics CONFIRMED directly from dre.ca.gov's own pages (examinees/BrokerExamContent.html, examinees/TakingExam.html) and the official Examination Description form RE 425 (Rev. 6/25), fetched and read directly from dre.ca.gov: the broker exam is 200 multiple-choice questions over 4 hours with a 75% passing score (vs. the salesperson exam's 150 questions / 3 hours / 70%), administered as a single unified exam with no separate national/state portions. RE 425 confirms both the salesperson and broker exams share the identical seven-area content outline -- Area 1 Property Ownership & Land Use Controls (~15%), Area 2 Laws of Agency & Fiduciary Duties (~17%), Area 3 Property Valuation & Financial Analysis (~14%), Area 4 Financing (~9%), Area 5 Transfer of Property (~8%), Area 6 Practice of Real Estate & Disclosures incl. Specialty Areas (~25%, the single largest area, covering trust account management, agency supervision, fair housing, property management, and mandated disclosures), and Area 7 Contracts (~12%) -- but DRE states the two exams 'differ in the emphasis and difficulty' by license level; this bank leans its question weighting into that broker-specific depth, concentrating extra volume in broker supervision/office management, trust fund handling, and property management/landlord-tenant law (together ~32% of this bank's 285 questions), consistent with the user's brief that broker content should emphasize landlord-tenant law, trust funds, and brokerage/office management. Real statute/regulation citations used throughout include Business and Professions Code Sections 10145, 10148, 10159.2, 10176, 10177, 10137, 10140.6, 10162-10163 (Real Estate Law and broker supervision/discipline), 10 CCR Sections 2725, 2726, 2831-2832, 2835.1 (Commissioner's Regulations on supervision and trust funds), Civil Code Sections 1102 et seq. (TDS), 1103 et seq. (NHDS), 1675 (liquidated damages cap), 1950.5 as amended by AB 12 effective 7/1/2024 (security deposit cap, confirmed via multiple corroborating legal-industry sources -- not a DRE page but well-corroborated and current law), 1946.1/1946.2/1947.12 (AB 1482 Tenant Protection Act just-cause/rent-cap), 1954 (landlord entry notice), 2079 et seq. (agency disclosure/Easton duty), 2924 et seq. (non-judicial foreclosure), and Code of Civil Procedure Sections 580b/580d (anti-deficiency); real estate math questions (GRM, cap rate/NOI, LTV, points, commission splits, proration, Prop 13 assessment mechanics) are grounded in standard, verifiable appraisal/finance formulas rather than any single hedged source. A handful of narrower operational figures (the $200 broker-personal-funds trust account allowance, the 45-hour/4-year CE renewal cycle and its seven mandatory subject areas, the 2-year salesperson experience + 8-course broker education prerequisite, the $50,000/$250,000 Recovery Fund caps) are corroborated by DRE's own public pages and licensing-industry sources but were not re-verified against the current numbered Code of Regulations text itself in this pass -- flagged in-content as DRE/industry guidance rather than presented as directly pinpoint-cited regulation text. Price set at $29.99 (2999 cents) to match this project's current standardized going rate for Real Estate tracks (applied project-wide since 2026-08-13), appropriate for a comprehensive 285-question broker-tier bank aimed at licensed salespersons upgrading credentials. Answer choices were drafted correct-as-choice_a throughout, then deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_ca_re_broker_answers.js (global sequential-cycle rotation, not manual), landing at A 25.3% / B 24.9% / C 24.9% / D 24.9% -- within this project's target band.
